content.thinking:
I’ve just gotten the server to start, but it keeps binding to a new port each time because the previous process isn’t fully terminated. The last command I ran (`kill %1`) only killed the most recent background job in this shell, but there may be other stray Node processes still listening on the earlier ports (3000, 3001). When I restarted, the server ended up on port 3002, which indicates that ports 3000 and 3001 are still occupied. This is why the banner printed twice earlier and why the API test was hitting the wrong port.

My goal now is to ensure there is exactly one server instance running, preferably on the original default port (3000) if it’s free, otherwise on the next available port, and then verify that the seeded games data is being served correctly. To do that I need to:

1. Kill any lingering Node processes that were started with `server/index.js`. Using `pkill -f "node server/index.js"` is a reliable way to terminate all such processes regardless of how they were started (background job, separate terminal, etc.).
2. Give the system a short pause so the OS can release the ports.
3. Start the server fresh with `nohup node server/index.js > /tmp/glint.log 2>&1 &`. This will capture the startup logs in a known file.
4. Wait a moment for the server to bind, then output the log to confirm which port it actually listened on.
5. After confirming the server is up, query the `/api/games` endpoint to ensure the seeded games are being returned. The previous curl command showed a partial JSON; I want a clean verification. I’ll pipe the JSON through a short Python one‑liner that loads the JSON and prints just the list of game names, making the output concise and easy to read.

All these steps can be combined into a single Bash command: first `pkill`, then `sleep`, then `nohup … &`, another `sleep`, then `cat` the log, then a separator, then the `curl | python3` pipeline. This will both clean up any stale processes and give me immediate confirmation that the server is running correctly and serving the expected data.

Thus, the appropriate tool call is a Bash execution with the composed command and a descriptive label.

arguments.command: pkill -f "node server/index.js" 2>/dev/null; sleep 0.8; nohup node server/index.js > /tmp/glint.log 2>&1 & sleep 1.5; cat /tmp/glint.log; echo "---"; curl -s http://localhost:3001/api/games | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print([g['name'] for g in d['games']])"
arguments.description: Kill stale servers, restart, verify seeded games
